overview:
Georgia's 13th District is among the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points. The open-seat contest features Jasmine Clark, who has raised over $2.3 million and drawn more than $4.2 million in outside support, against Republican Jonathan Chavez, who reports no significant fundraising. No general-election polls are available, and national rating organizations have not listed the race.

Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 97 percent, and the district's fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s. With no outside spending opposing Clark and a financial advantage measured in the millions, the seat remains firmly in Democratic hands barring an unexpected shift. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty stemming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of competitive conditions.
